correctness.rationale: At n<=3 there is no solution, n=4 and n=7 are the exceptional solutions. For even n, an odd prime factor of n=2u forces Omega(n+2)>=3, except n=4. For odd n with both endpoint Omega<=2, systematically eliminate prime/prime, prime/square, square/prime, semiprime/prime, prime/semiprime, both squares, square/semiprime and semiprime/square by the totient and product/sum identities or AM-GM. In the remaining distinct-odd-semiprime case n=pq, n+2=rs, equality of totients and product difference give r+s=p+q+2; ordered prime gaps e=s-r,d=q-p satisfy e^2-d^2=4(p+q-1). Therefore A=(e-d)/2, B=(e+d)/2 are uniquely determined odd integers 3<=A<B, with the four prime formulas in pinned RESULT.md. Direct expansion gives rs=pq+2 and equal totients in the converse. The result is genuinely unbounded in n; enumeration only cross-checks. Independent Euler totient/sieve through n=250000 found precisely 4,7,6497,12317,133787,181427 with nontrivial pairs (A,B)=(7,23),(13,17),(17,43),(23,37).

originality.rationale: The exact biconditional covers ALL separately low-Omega endpoint types and uniquely inverts a two-parameter prime quadruple. Graham–Holt–Pomerance 1999 already gives a four-prime family, and for gap two its construction is precisely A=3, so that special case receives no novelty credit. Their Theorem 1 yields another class and is not a complete classification of the low-Omega layer. Ford studies the fixed-gap problem generally. An OEIS solution list is not a symbolic exhaustive classifier. Best-of-knowledge no source inspected dominates the full result; a hidden elementary classification remains possible.
